title: The 15-Minute Loaded Baked Potato Soup That Saved My Cold Weeknights
description: Make a cozy loaded baked potato soup in just 15 minutes. Save money with this easy, comforting Aldi-friendly recipe that beats restaurant takeout.
story: Working late in my chilly apartment last Tuesday, the absolute last thing I wanted to do was chop veggies for an hour. Honestly, I was this close to ordering delivery from the local pub—until I saw the $25 bill staring back at me on my phone screen. Nope! I raided my fridge instead and pulled together this loaded baked potato soup in right around 15 minutes using a bag of russet potatoes from Aldi and some leftover cheddar. It cost me maybe $4 total to feed myself, and it warmed me right up to my bones. The first time I tested this, I cranked the skillet way too high and scorched the bottom of my pot—keep the heat medium-low once the milk goes in so everything stays velvety smooth. If you need a fast, budget-friendly bowl of pure comfort tonight, this is it.
ingredients: 3 medium russet potatoes, peeled and diced small so they cook fast
2 cups chicken broth (plus a splash more if it gets too thick)
1 cup sharp cheddar cheese, freshly shredded (Trader Joe's cheddar is my go-to)
4 slices of bacon, crisped up and crumbled
3 green onions, thinly sliced for topping
Kosher salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Step 1: Melt the Kerrygold butter in a medium soup pot over medium heat. Toss in the diced russet potatoes and let them sauté for about 3 minutes until they start smelling earthy and golden on the edges.
Step 2: Sprinkle the flour directly over the potatoes, stirring constantly for 1 minute to cook out that raw flour taste. It'll look pasty, and that's totally normal.
Step 3: Pour in the chicken broth and whole milk while whisking so no lumps form. Bring it to a gentle simmer, pop a lid on, and let it bubble for 8 minutes until the potatoes are fork-tender.

Step 4: Mash about half of the potatoes right in the pot with a potato masher or fork to get that thick, creamy texture. Stir in the shredded cheddar until melted, then top with crumbled bacon and green onions before serving.
proHack: Don't use pre-shredded bagged cheese if you can help it! The anti-caking powders they coat it with will make your soup grainy instead of silky. Grating a block of sharp cheddar takes 60 seconds and makes a huge difference.
storage: Store leftover soup in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat it gently on the stovetop over low heat with a splash of milk to bring back that creamy texture, as it thickens up quite a bit overnight.

faqs.question: Can I substitute milk if I don't have heavy cream or whole milk?
faqs.answer: Totally! You can use evaporated milk, or even a dairy-free oat milk if that's what you keep in your fridge. Just avoid skim milk or the soup might taste a bit watery.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the cheese from clumping up into a ball?
faqs.answer: Turn your burner down to low or completely off before stirring in the cheese. Excessive heat makes dairy separate and get stringy, so let the residual heat of the soup melt the cheese gently.
